tagline: Over the Warners, past the dune-rimmed lakes, toward Steens.
intro: The byway leaves US 395 at OR 140 north of Lakeview and crosses the Warner Mountains, then comes down into the Warner Valley, where marshes and shallow lakes spread out around Plush. From there it crosses Hart Mountain, a geologic escarpment, and runs east over a broad high desert with Steens Mountain far off, to meet OR 205 south of Frenchglen, about 90 miles in all.
Crescent dunes line the north shores of the Warner lakes, built up by swings between wet years and dry, and the BLM says the only other lake complex like it is in South Africa.

moments.title: Plush
moments.text: The name is said to come from a flush mispronounced over a 19th-century poker game, and in 1898 a Daniel Boone, kin to the Kentucky pathfinder, became the postmaster.

moments.title: Hart Mountain National Antelope Refuge
moments.text: Set aside in 1936 for the remnant herds of pronghorn, the refuge is among the largest wildlife habitats with no domestic livestock, and bighorn sheep and golden eagles share it.

practical: The byway is all-weather road, about 40 miles paved and 50 graveled and fit for passenger cars, though winter storms can close it for short spells, and most roads inside the refuge are primitive.
